papers.text: A spotting step by the shops. You go first, and ideally see a bus.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Window boxes for the town hall. Flowers only. A leek has applied.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A show results board by the shops. Last year's results to follow.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A warm seat by the shops. Between us we have waited eleven years.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plinth for the winner of Window Week. The winner is a window.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Cabbages round the bus stop, with a sign: QUIET, WE ARE GROWING.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A light by the plots for late buses. Pumpkins asked to be kept in the dark.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A high street glass case for the pumpkin. You would unveil it, slowly.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Awnings for the shops and the timetable. Cloud dims a window 30 %.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Let us sit in the Guild's window at bus times. We keep very still.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The Society's cold frames, for our hats. Sign: GROWN UNDER GLASS.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Turnips are 12 % more turnip in early spring. Move Window Week.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A right of way across the vegetable plots, from 8:14 to 8:16.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Two spotters for show day, to write down weights. Buses go unwritten.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The bus station waiting room, for Till's Teas. We wait on people.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for the clock to chime at every bus: about forty a day.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The pumpkin would like a spot in the hat window. It used the hat form.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: The bus stop is glass on three sides. By Guild rules, a window. Ours.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Till's Teas will pay to print the timetable, plus a tea break at 10:15.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will hire the high street to read the timetable aloud. Then the footnotes.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Till's Teas will pay to sponsor the show cup. As a teacup.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will hire Till's Teas for the pumpkin's birthday. It is one.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bus stop for seedlings. Then the shelter. Then a bus.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Present our prize for most buses seen, Mayor. Be pictured seeing one.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Say in public that the 8:15 ran on time. It nearly did.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Judge Window Week, Mayor. Admire each window, not yourself in it.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Our prize turnip asks for your name, Mayor. It has your bearing.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Attend the weigh-in, Mayor, and say 'goodness'. We will cue you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A study of the founding napkin. A timetable may be on the back.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The napkin study found the timetable. It asks to find out if it still runs.

papers.text: We propose a study of why our last study took nine years. It should take about ten.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study of the study recommends a third study, to be sure.

papers.text: What is a vegetable? A working group will take evidence at lunch.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The working group has taken its evidence. It asks a year more, for pudding.

papers.text: A committee to name the benches by the plots. Then one per bench.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bench committee asks for a third bench, to hold its meetings on.

papers.text: A study of the seconds a passer-by gives a window. Three years.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Our study's answer is four. It asks for another year to find out four what.

papers.text: A review of the duck pond. So far: wet, ducks. Two more meetings.
papers.subject: ducks
papers.biggerStudy: Two more meetings were not enough. The ducks have asked to be heard.

papers.text: Your hats on show in the hall, Mayor, each with a plaque: WORN.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Name the duck pond after you. The ducks will be told in writing.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: Your portrait at every bus stop, Mayor, captioned PLEASE WAIT.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A desk fountain for you. It gets lonely. A friend on the high street?
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it would like the Society's best rain barrel to drink from.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S DESK FOUNTAIN TAKES GROWERS' RAIN BARREL
clippings.refuse: DESK FOUNTAIN TOLD TO FIND ITS OWN WATER

papers.text: Another basket, to keep the first company. No reason, as before.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the second basket: it would like the top deck's front seat. Daily.

clippings.sign: BASKET TAKES FRONT SEAT OF TOP DECK; SPOTTERS STAND

papers.text: A hat for Mondays. We have six more, one a day. No obligation.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it would like the Guild's front window. Centre, well lit.

clippings.sign: HAT TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW; GUILD SPEECHLESS
clippings.refuse: HAT GOES BACK IN ITS BOX, SAYS NOTHING
